units: <cite ref="Ketubot 85b:7">Keth. 85ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ ותלמיד חכם וכ׳</he> if a neighbor (of the deceased) and a scholar (of the same name claim a legacy), the scholar is preferred; <cite ref="Bava Metzia 108b:9">B. Mets. 108ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ ותלמיד וכ׳</he> if a neighbor and a scholar want to buy a field, the scholar has the preemption.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:7">Ab. I, 7</cite> <he>הרחק מש׳ רע</he> keep away from a bad neighbor.

<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 12:6">Neg. XII, 6</cite> (prov.) <he>אוי לרשע אוי לשְׁכֵנוֹ</he> woe to the wicked, and woe to his neighbor; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18:22">Num. R. s. 18<sup>5</sup></cite>; a. fr.—Y. Ab. Zar. II, end, 42ᵃ (mixed dict.) <he>ש׳ חד הוה לנא וכ׳</he> we had one (gentile) neighbor &c.—Pl. <he>שְׁכֵנִים</he>, <he>שְׁכֵי׳</he>. Keth. l. c. <he>שניהם קרובים ושניהם ש׳ וכ׳</he> if both claimants are relatives (of the deceased), or both neighbors, or both scholars, it is left to the discretion of the judges (v. <cite ref="U00334"><he>שׁוּדָא</he></cite>). B. Mets. l. c. <he>שְׁכֵינֵי העיר ושְׁכֵינֵי שדה וכ׳</he> if neighbors in the town and neighbors in the field (want to buy a field), the city neighbors have the pre-emption.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 1:4">Sot. I, 4</cite> (address to the suspected adulteress) <he>הרבה ש׳ הרעים וכ׳</he> bad neighbors do much (may have influenced you).
Keth. 72ᵃ שמשיאתו שם רע בשְׁכֵינָיו she is the cause of his bearing a bad name among his neighbors; a. fr.—Fem. שְׁכֵנָה, שְׁכֵי׳.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 2:8:3">Y. Bets. II, end, 61ᵈ</cite> <he>שְׁכֵינָתוֹ היתה</he> it was his neighbor’s wife that did it; <he>ויש … על שכינתו</he> is a man punished for what his neighboress does?; a. e.—Pl. <he>שְׁכֵינוֹת</he>. Keth. l. c. <he>משיאה … בשְׁכֵיניֹתֶיהָ</he> he is the cause of her bearing a bad name among her neighbors; a. e.
